observation: Pandemic disruption, project delays, logistics dislocation, supply constraints, raw-material inflation and cost-control pressure contributed to a £2.1m adjusted EBITDA loss and £5.8m pre-tax loss for the extended period, versus £4.7m adjusted EBITDA and £2.0m pre-tax profit in the prior twelve months. Cash was £3.5m after drawing the £3.0m CBILS loan and £3.0m trade facility. Forecast liquidity relied on renewals not yet formally agreed, creating a material going-concern uncertainty. Management was already restructuring the business and executing a broad improvement programme, while the December 2021 order book reached a record £20.3m.
already_announced_exclusion: The restructuring already underway, leadership and personnel changes, commercial-governance and bid-process changes, integration, business-improvement programme, cost controls and bank-facility actions disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Operating losses, market disruption and explicit reliance on unagreed facility renewals support very high pressure scores. Record orders, major contract wins and long-term market growth provide meaningful but incomplete contrary evidence.

observation: Revenue increased 32% to £39.9m and the adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to £0.3m, but the statutory pre-tax loss widened to £9.9m after a £4.7m Offshore Energy goodwill impairment. Offshore Energy lost £2.1m of adjusted EBITDA; project delays, supply-chain escalation and two legacy contracts weakened margins. Cash was £5.2m and net debt £1.4m, while the auditor identified material going-concern uncertainty because working capital relied on banking facilities due for renewal. A £5.3m equity raise and conditional £18m convertible facility had stabilised the balance sheet. Organisational efficiencies, integration and £0.8m annualised cost removal were already implemented; the January 2024 order book was £19.7m at improved margin.
already_announced_exclusion: The April 2023 strategic investment and equity raise, conditional convertible facility, organisational-efficiency programme, support-function and engineering integration, £0.8m annualised cost removal, supply-chain savings and legacy-contract remediation disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Improving revenue and EBITDA coexist with a larger statutory loss, impairment, divisional losses, project and margin pressure and material going-concern uncertainty. Stronger funding, improved order-book margin and a stated path to profitability provide substantial but incomplete contrary evidence.
